findings.message: Decision: Option D (layered chain) — DADAIA_AGENT_PERSONA env var > harness-specific env vars (CLAUDE_/CODEX_/OPENCODE_AGENT_PERSONA) > tool_input._meta.agent_persona payload field > fail-open. Persona resolution is harness-agnostic at the gate level; shim is one-line per harness.
Cache strategy: per-invocation in-process only (single frontmatter read per hook process). No file-backed cache, no daemon. Cost well under NFR2's 50 ms budget.

Fail-open log line literal: '[<iso8601>] sdd-gate: FAIL-OPEN path-scope: no agent persona detected (env=unset payload=unset) tool=<TOOL> path=<FPATH>'. Retention inherits /tmp/ auto-purge; gate must not rotate.

Trade-off accepted: fail-open at step 6 bypasses the step-7 TASKS-marker gate for top-level human invocations. Humans no longer need a [-] marker for production-path edits. This is intentional per SPEC §FR2.4; document operator-visibly.

Until each harness's sub-agent runner exports DADAIA_AGENT_PERSONA (one-line shim), path-scope protection is dormant — every agent invocation fails open. Software-engineer is unblocked to land AGT-r2-19; PE must document the shim in data/AGENTS.md §'Agent persona contract' under AGT-r2-33.

decisions_required: software-engineer (AGT-r2-19): implement the layered-chain resolver and the step-6 path-scope branch in dadaia_workspace/public/scripts/sdd-spec-gate.sh per §3 §7 §8 of this report.
software-engineer (AGT-r2-20): land tests/unit/gate/test_path_scope.py with the 9 mandatory cases T1–T9 (T10 optional) per §9 of this report.
product-engineer (AGT-r2-33): document the DADAIA_AGENT_PERSONA env var contract in data/AGENTS.md §'Agent persona contract' so each harness's sub-agent runner knows what to set.
product-engineer (AGT-r2-49): record in specs/memory/architecture.html §'layers' that the path-scope gate is a fail-open guardrail (not a security boundary).
